name: Work Residency Visa / Employment License

requirements.blocker_text: Foreigners cannot work without a license from the competent authority, and employers cannot hire non-nationals without prior government approval. In most sectors, at least 75% of an employer's workforce must be Libyan nationals (temporarily reducible if qualified nationals are unavailable) -- meaning foreign staff are capped at roughly 25% of the workforce. Employment contracts must be in Arabic and approved by the competent authority. Special carve-outs exist for medical professionals (via hospital cooperation agreements) and the oil sector (via a dedicated office).
requirements.fix_path: Secure a Libyan employer's sponsorship, obtain the government work license, and ensure the hire fits within the employer's Libyan-national workforce quota.

evidence_required.document: Arabic-language employment contract approved by the competent authority

outcome.duration_length: tied to the work residency visa's validity, set case-by-case by the competent authority

sources.title: ICMPD (International Centre for Migration Policy Development, an intergovernmental organization) -- The Legal Guide for Foreigners in Libya (January 2020): work licensing, 75% Libyanization quota, contract requirements, residency fees

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Libya). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier 2 (an intergovernmental organization's legal guide, not a .gov.ly government text; no Libyan government source could be reached in this build, and given the country's fragmented governance since 2014, it is unclear a single authoritative government portal even exists). GENUINE, COMPARABLE QUOTA FINDING: a 75% Libyan-national workforce minimum (foreign staff capped near 25%) sits between Bolivia's 15%-foreign-cap (85% local minimum, the strictest found in this dataset) and Angola's 30%-foreign-cap (70% local minimum, the most permissive) -- Libya's rule is the middle point of the three quota figures found across this session. No PR ladder is confirmed for this route (see ly_residence_permit.json's own note on the absence of a tiered residence system, unlike Cameroon or Congo-Brazzaville); citizenship_after_months reflects the general 10-year naturalization requirement (see ly_citizenship_naturalisation.json), not a work-permit-specific accelerated path.
